newsitem.title: USA: Travelers Property earnings seen growing.
newsitem.headline: Travelers Property earnings seen growing.

text.p: Travelers Property Casualty Corp should see impressive earnings growth for the next few quarters after first quarter earnings exceeded market expectations five percent, analysts said.
The gains resulted primarily from cost reductions.

Travelers Property Casualty, which is an 82 percent owned subsidiary of Travelers Group, should continue to benefit from investment income growth and solid performance in its personal lines business, analysts said.
Travelers Property Casualty on Monday reported first quarter operating earnings of $0.67 per share, up from $0.27 per share a year earlier.
The positive earnings surprise prompted some analysts to upgrade their projections for the rest of the year.
"I've raised my 1997 earnings estimate to $2.75 from $2.70," said Weston Hicks, senior research analyst at Sanford C. Bernstein & Co.
Hicks said his firm was recommending Travelers Property Casualty as an investment.
"The reason is that they are moving to a low-cost position in a consolidating industry, which could have a very significant payoff if they can make some additional acquisitions," Hicks said.
Travelers Property Chairman and Chief Executive Robert Lipp said: "Earnings were strong and we are fast approaching our goal of $300 million in annualized expense savings."

The company was created in April 1996 after Travelers Group bought Aetna Inc's property-casualty business for about $4 billion. Since the acquisition, Travelers has trimmed jobs and operating costs as it combined the two big operations.
Travelers Group Chairman Sanford Weill has said the company is on the lookout for further property-casualty acquisitions.
Travelers has a reputation for growing by acquiring other companies and it likes companies where it can cut expenses and boost profitability almost immediately, analysts said.
Stuart Shaw, co-managing partner at Branche Research Group, said Travelers Property Casualty was making good use of the sales force of sister company Primerica Financial Services (PFS).

"What I think is a long-term sleeper that's starting to grow is the auto and homeowners insurance that's being sold by PFS," Shaw said. "That's just a small part right now, but it could be quite a good growth opportunity going forward.
"This management is going to be very selective in growing the top line and is very much focused on profitability."
